Construct a weighted gene co-expression network and detect modules

rna_wgcna.Rd

Constructs a weighted gene co-expression network using normalized expression data stored in an rna_project object and identifies gene co-expression modules using the WGCNA framework.

The function filters genes with zero or invalid variance, optionally retains the most variable genes, performs expression-data quality control, constructs the network using a predefined soft-thresholding power, and detects modules through hierarchical clustering of the topological overlap matrix (TOM).

Module assignments, module eigengenes, network information, and analysis metadata are organized into a result object. Diagnostic dendrogram plots can also be generated to visualize the identified modules.

Usage

rna_wgcna(
  project,
  power,
  genes_n = 10000,
  network_type = c("signed", "unsigned", "signed hybrid"),
  tom_type = c("signed", "unsigned", "unsigned 2", "signed Nowick", "signed Nowick 2"),
  cor_method = "pearson",
  max_block_size = 20000,
  min_module_size = 30,
  deep_split = 2,
  merge_cut_height = 0.25,
  reassign_threshold = 1e-06,
  numeric_labels = FALSE,
  pam_respects_dendro = FALSE,
  threads = NULL,
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

An rna_project object containing normalized gene expression data and sample metadata.

power

Numeric value specifying the soft-thresholding power used to construct the network. This value should be selected beforehand using rna_pick_power or another appropriate diagnostic approach. Must be finite and positive.

genes_n

Integer or NULL. Maximum number of genes to retain, selected by decreasing expression variance across samples. Genes with non-finite or zero variance are excluded before selection. If NULL, all eligible genes are retained. Using a subset of the most variable genes can reduce computational requirements. Defaults to 10000.

network_type

Character string specifying the network type used by WGCNA. Supported values are "signed", "unsigned", and "signed hybrid". A signed network preserves the distinction between positive and negative correlations; an unsigned network uses the magnitude of correlations; and a signed hybrid network excludes negative correlations from the adjacency calculation. Defaults to "signed".

tom_type

Character string specifying the type of topological overlap matrix (TOM) used for module detection. Supported values are "signed", "unsigned", "unsigned 2", "signed Nowick", and "signed Nowick 2". This parameter controls how topological overlap is calculated and is independent of the adjacency network type specified by network_type. Defaults to "signed".

cor_method

Character string specifying the correlation method used during network construction. Currently supports "pearson", which is also used in downstream calculations of module membership (kME) to ensure consistency with the original network. Defaults to "pearson".

max_block_size

Integer specifying the maximum number of genes allowed in each block during network construction. When the number of genes exceeds this limit, WGCNA divides the data into multiple blocks and constructs networks separately. Larger values may increase memory requirements. Defaults to 20000.

min_module_size

Integer specifying the minimum number of genes required to form a module during dynamic tree cutting. Smaller modules are generally not retained as independent modules. Defaults to 30.

deep_split

Integer between 0 and 4 controlling the sensitivity of dynamic tree cutting. Higher values generally produce more modules by allowing finer subdivisions of the gene dendrogram. Higher values correspond to more aggressive module detection. Defaults to 2.

merge_cut_height

Numeric value between 0 and 1 specifying the threshold for merging modules based on the dissimilarity between their module eigengenes. Lower values result in more conservative merging, whereas higher values allow more modules to be merged. Defaults to 0.25.

reassign_threshold

Numeric value between 0 and 1 specifying the threshold used for gene reassignment based on module membership significance during module detection. A value of 0 disables reassignment based on this threshold. Defaults to 1e-6.

numeric_labels

Logical. If TRUE, modules are represented by numeric labels in the network result. If FALSE, modules are represented by their assigned colors. The returned genes_modules table also includes module colors regardless of this setting. Defaults to FALSE.

pam_respects_dendro

Logical. Specifies whether the partitioning around medoids (PAM) stage of module detection must respect the dendrogram produced by hierarchical clustering. If TRUE, PAM assignments are constrained by the dendrogram; if FALSE, genes may be assigned to modules independently of their position in the dendrogram. Defaults to FALSE.

threads

Integer or NULL. Number of threads used during network construction. If NULL, the nThreads argument is omitted and WGCNA uses its default behavior. A positive integer specifies the number of threads passed to the network construction procedure. Defaults to NULL.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, generates diagnostic dendrogram plots showing the module color assignments for each network block. Defaults to TRUE.

save

Logical. If TRUE, attaches the network result to the project under the analyses slot with subtype "wgcna_network" and invisibly returns the updated project. If FALSE, does not attach the result and instead invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_network_result. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

If save = TRUE, invisibly returns the updated rna_project object containing the network result.

If save = FALSE, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_network_result, containing:

  • network: the complete network object returned by blockwiseModules.

  • genes_modules: a data frame containing gene identifiers, module labels, and module colors.

  • MEs: the ordered module eigengene matrix.

  • Network construction parameters, including the soft-thresholding power and network types.

  • The number and identifiers of retained genes and samples.

  • Identifiers of genes excluded due to invalid variance, gene selection, or WGCNA quality control, and samples removed during quality control.

  • timestamp: the date and time of analysis.

Input data

The expression matrix must be numeric, with genes in rows and samples in columns. Gene identifiers and sample identifiers must be unique.

The metadata must identify samples through a Sample column or through its row names. Sample identifiers are matched to the expression matrix column names; metadata must contain an entry for every expression sample.

Genes with non-finite or zero variance are excluded before the most variable genes are selected. WGCNA quality control is then applied to identify and remove additional problematic samples or genes.

Network construction

The network is constructed using the adjacency function and topological overlap matrix defined by network_type and tom_type, respectively. The soft-thresholding power specified by power is applied to the adjacency calculation.

When the number of selected genes exceeds max_block_size, WGCNA may divide the data into multiple blocks. Module detection is performed independently within each block, and the resulting module assignments are returned in a unified result object.

Modules are identified through hierarchical clustering and dynamic tree cutting. Closely related modules may subsequently be merged according to merge_cut_height.

Module eigengenes

Module eigengenes are calculated by WGCNA as part of the module detection procedure. They represent the first principal component of the expression profiles of genes assigned to each module and provide a summarized representation of module-level expression patterns.

The returned eigengene matrix is ordered using orderMEs. Additional analyses, such as module membership (kME) estimation and associations between module eigengenes and sample-level phenotypes, can be performed in subsequent steps.

Interpretation

Identified modules represent groups of genes with similar expression patterns across the samples included in the analysis. Module detection depends on the selected soft-thresholding power, network type, TOM definition, and module detection parameters.

Module colors are arbitrary identifiers assigned by WGCNA and do not have intrinsic biological meaning. Biological interpretation requires additional analyses, such as functional enrichment, module membership evaluation, and associations with relevant phenotypes.

The resulting modules describe co-expression relationships across the samples supplied in the project as a whole. They do not directly represent differential co-expression between experimental groups or establish causal relationships between genes.

Scope of the analysis

This function constructs a single co-expression network using all retained samples. It does not perform differential co-expression analysis, consensus network construction, module preservation analysis, or phenotype association testing. These analyses require additional steps.

References

Langfelder P, Horvath S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559
